changes.before: The sign at the creek had said eight.
changes.after: She had read eight sets of tracks at the creek.

changes.before: He knew she would make him ride rather than make herself talk, so he rode, sitting deep in the saddle as if this were what he'd intended all along.
changes.after: He rode it out at her side, sitting deep in the saddle, the reins still slack in one hand.

changes.before: A day, she thought. Two if she was careful.
changes.after: A day. Two if she was careful.

changes.before: He said nothing. He only tilted his head, the way he had over the dead troll when she named the southern stones.
changes.after: He tilted his head, the way he had over the dead troll when she named the southern stones.

changes.before: She had told him nothing about where to ride; he had dropped into place a length off the mare's left hip, as a junior ranger would.
changes.after: He had taken the junior's place a length off the mare's left hip.

changes.before: Cyndia said it straight out, which was the thing Sylvanas had always valued in her.
In the cold ward-light Sylvanas could see every hard line of her face.
changes.after: The cold ward-light showed every hard line of her face.

changes.before: Her hands were clasped in her lap, gripping her own fingers hard enough to whiten them.
changes.after: She sat with her hands clasped in her lap, gripping her own fingers hard enough to whiten them.

changes.before: The mage had to tip her head back to meet her, and she did.
changes.after: The mage had to tip her head back, and she did, chin up.

changes.before: From here Sylvanas could see what she had missed from the doorway. The eyes were blue,
changes.after: At this range, the eyes were blue,
changes.note: Gate suggested 'Up close,'; adjusted to 'At this range,' because 'Up close' already opens line 23 ('Up close the troll smelled worse').
